'''2001 Vegas DPC''' was a Star Wars CCG Decipher Pro Circuit tournament held in Las Vegas, Nevada in 2001. [[Brian Hunter]] won it.<ref name="dt-15676">[http://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/15676 DeckTech post 15676], DeckTech (Brian "HuntaWarya" Hunter, 1 May 2001). Preservation copies: [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/15676/ Stephen Skilton]; [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/15676/ GitHub Pages].</ref><ref name="dt-15742">[http://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/15742 Really no order with Imps involved], DeckTech (Tim "Info Broker" Guzman, 3 May 2001). Preservation copies: [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/15742/ Stephen Skilton]; [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/15742/ GitHub Pages].</ref>

* '''Dates:''' 28 April 2001<ref name="tr-d2191" />
* '''Site:''' Las Vegas, Nevada; Thomas and Mack Center, Las Vegas, Nevada<ref name="tr-d2191" />
* '''Format:''' [[Premiere - Reflections II]]
* '''Winner:''' [[Brian Hunter]]
* '''Players:''' about 72<ref name="tr-d2202" />

The event is known from players' DeckTech posts; they give no exact date. It was played before the [[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]] expansion was released on 30 May 2001. For the next year's event see [[2002 Vegas DPC]].

Hunter won with a Dark ISB Operations space deck; his posted list is not card for card what he played, since at Vegas he ran the combo version of Ghhhk, to cancel Landing Claw, with Masterful Move; the posted list has Captain Godherdt in place of Masterful Move.<ref name="dt-15676" /> Guzman took 7th place with his Dark space Court deck, built from an idea of Alex's from Canada.<ref name="dt-15742" /> Montgomery's Dark deck lost only once at the DPC, by seven; Ira Babb later took the same deck to Texas states and placed 5th.<ref name="dt-15723" /> Marshall added Control & SFS to his Hunt Down deck for the DPC and wrote that it won him two games; he refers readers to his Vegas DPC report for game 7, against Scott Anderson's Profit.<ref name="dt-16285" />

== Discrepancies ==

Where a source disagrees with the record on this page, the page keeps the record and notes the difference here.

* Jared Arthur reports his round 3 game against Caleb Smith as a full win by 14; Caleb Smith reports the same game (his round 3) as a full loss by 4.<ref name="tr-d2230" />
* Jared Arthur reports his round 3 game against Caleb Smith as a full win by 14; Caleb Smith reports the same game (his round 3) as a full loss by 4.<ref name="tr-d2235" />
* Steve Marshall reports that Brian Hunter won the first final game against Chris Shaner by 18; Hunter's own report gives that game as a win by 8.<ref name="tr-d2268" />
